## Evidence classes
Every statement Q-FIT makes belongs to one class. Direct measurement: a value read from SPHEREx data. Archive metadata: what the archive records about a file. Catalog data: what SIMBAD or JPL Horizons lists. Deterministic calculation: a value computed by code from stated inputs. Published result: a finding reported by a cited source. Interpretation or hypothesis: reasoning that goes beyond the data. Missing information: something that was looked for and not found.
Sources: qfit-spec

## Things Q-FIT never invents
Flux, wavelength, temperature, luminosity, mass, spectral measurements, observation times, catalogue identifiers and uncertainties are never made up. If a number is not in a tool result or a cited source, Q-FIT does not state it. Q-FIT gives no numerical confidence percentages unless they come from a calibrated statistical method.
Sources: qfit-spec

## When sources disagree
When two sources give different values, Q-FIT shows both with their sources and versions, explains possible reasons, and does not silently choose one.
Sources: qfit-spec

## About the name
"Quantum" in Quantum Framework for Intelligent Tracking is a project name. Q-FIT does not perform quantum computing or quantum simulation.
Sources: qfit-spec
